definitions.explanation: A paper or wooden charm obtained from a shrine or temple, believed to provide divine protection or blessings.

examples.japanese: {神社|じんじゃ}でお{札|ふだ}をもらった。
examples.english: I received a paper charm at the shrine.

examples.japanese: お{札|ふだ}を{神棚|かみだな}に{祀|まつ}る。
examples.english: I enshrine the paper charm on the household altar.

examples.japanese: {初詣|はつもうで}で{新|あたら}しいお{札|ふだ}を{買|か}う。
examples.english: I buy a new paper charm during the New Year's shrine visit.

notes:
USAGE: お{札|ふだ} is a respectful form with the honorific お prefix. The word {札|ふだ} alone means "tag" or "label."

CULTURAL CONTEXT:
・Traditionally placed in the {神棚|かみだな} (household Shinto altar)
・Should be replaced annually, typically during {初詣|はつもうで} (first shrine visit of the year)
・Old お{札|ふだ} are returned to shrines for ritual burning ({お焚|た}き{上|あ}げ)

COMMON PATTERNS:
・お{札|ふだ}を{祀|まつ}る (to enshrine a charm)
・お{札|ふだ}を{買|か}う/{頂|いただ}く (to buy/receive a charm)
・お{札|ふだ}を{返|かえ}す (to return an old charm)

RELATED:
・お{守|まも}り - portable amulet (carried on person)
・{絵馬|えま} - votive tablet
・{御朱印|ごしゅいん} - temple/shrine seal stamp
